record.original_question: Let G be a cubic planar graph and let L be a 3-list-assignment on G, meaning each vertex has a list of three allowed colors. An L-coloring is proper if adjacent vertices receive different colors, and two L-colorings are disjoint if every vertex receives different colors in the two colorings. Must every such 3-list-assignment admit two disjoint proper L-colorings?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a cubic planar graph (i.e., a planar graph in which every vertex has degree exactly 3). A list-assignment on $G$ is a function $L$ that assigns to each vertex $v \in V(G)$ a set $L(v)$ of allowed colors; it is a 3-list-assignment if $|L(v)| = 3$ for every $v$. An $L$-coloring of $G$ is a map $c: V(G) \to \mathbb{N}$ with $c(v) \in L(v)$ for every $v$; it is proper if $c(u) \neq c(v)$ whenever $uv \in E(G)$. Two $L$-colorings $c_1, c_2$ are called disjoint if $c_1(v) \neq c_2(v)$ for every $v \in V(G)$.

Question: Is it true that for every cubic planar graph $G$ and every 3-list-assignment $L$ on $G$, there exist two disjoint proper $L$-colorings of $G$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is part of a set of open problems on disjoint list-colorings (list packing) for planar graphs. Known positive results require additional girth assumptions: every 3-list-assignment on a planar graph of girth at least 8 admits two disjoint proper L-colorings, and fractional packings are known under girth ≥ 6. No proof or counterexample for the cubic planar case (without girth assumptions) was found in the available literature, so the problem appears to still be open.

status_evidence.title: Disjoint list-colorings for planar graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Two disjoint L-colorings are guaranteed for planar graphs of girth at least 8; fractional packing exists at girth ≥ 6.
status_evidence.claim: Disjoint 3-list-colorings for planar graphs are established only under girth conditions, leaving the cubic planar case unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Open problems of the 32nd Workshop on Cycles and Colourings (arXiv:2411.10046)
status_evidence.snippet: Contains open problems with notes on the current state of the art presented at the workshop.
status_evidence.claim: The question appears in a workshop open-problems collection, indicating it is presented as currently open.
